div.head: Iudex 9.1
div.ab: Hosticum potest aliquotiens homo fuga uel defensione uitare, prauos iudices non ita potest, quotiens aduersus subditos malis desideriis inflammantur.

Þa unrihtwisan deman hí beoð wyrsan þonne herigende here: here man mæg foroft befleon; ac þa deman for hira anwealde man ne mæg befleon, ðonne he him of hira ceastrewarena forðrycnesse gestreon gaderiað.
Unjust judges are worse than a plundering army. A man may often flee from an army, but from the power of judges no man can flee. Then they oppress the townspeople to gain profit.

Die ungerechten Richter, die sind schlimmer als verheerendes [Feindes]heer: vor einem Heere kann man gar oft flüchten; aber jenen Richtern kann wegen ihrer Amtsgewalt niemand entrinnen, sobald sie aus Erpressung ihrer Bürger sich Gewinn sammeln.

Unjust judges are worse than a ravaging [enemy] army: one can very often flee from an army; but from those judges, because of their official power, no one can escape when they gather gain for themselves by oppressing their citizens.
